description: Dual clock: major every 30s reorganises large wall sets; minor every 10s applies small local edits on top of whatever major state is active.

A.label: Base layout
A.description: The carved maze as generated — all original passages intact. Both clocks start from this state.

B-major.label: Major reorganisation
B-major.description: 14 internal walls toggled open. The south-east quadrant opens a new express route; the north-west closes two shortcuts. Player can be mid-corridor when this fires — anti-softlock nudge applies.

B-minor.label: Minor local edits
B-minor.description: 4 internal walls toggled open in the centre of the maze. Subtle enough that a moving player may not immediately notice, but halts dead-end predictions. Applied on top of whichever major state is currently active.

major.behavior: Alternates A ↔ B-major on every tick.

minor.behavior: Applies B-minor delta on top of whichever major state is active. Does NOT alternate — always the same 4 toggles, re-applied.

decoyExits.description: Two decoy exits placed on the perimeter. Each plays stinger_not_exit and a TTS line so the player can learn to distinguish them from the real exit (which plays stinger_success).

notes: Both clocks run independently — they can (and will) fire close together, creating a brief period of maximum confusion.
The minor clock fires 3 times per major cycle, so the player experiences: minor, minor, major+minor (same tick), minor, minor, major+minor ... etc.
Shift warnings (5 s before) are shown on the HUD for BOTH clocks but only the major fires a klaxon SFX.
Ghost walls (memory-glitch) are enabled for major shifts only to keep minor shifts subtle.
